summary: Depth-first rabbithole dossier for Replica Set Transactions; source-anchored research pack.

facts.text: [low] The Majority write concern waits for the write to be applied to a majority of replica set data-bearing and electable members, ensuring the write cannot be rolled back in the event of a primary election. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/blog/post/performance-best-practices-transactions-and-read--write-concerns

[high] Starting with MongoDB 4.0, support was added for multi-document ACID transactions on replica sets, enabling developers to address a complete range of use cases. (verified as of 2026-10-14) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/blog/post/performance-best-practices-transactions-and-read--write-concerns, https://severalnines.com/blog/transaction-considerations-mongodb-production/

[low] MongoDB supports a readConcern level of “Linearizable”, which ensures the node is still the primary member of the replica set at the time of the read and that the returned data will not be rolled back if another node is subsequently elected. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/blog/post/performance-best-practices-transactions-and-read--write-concerns
